Diagnostics of a fitted model

Source: R/report.R
diagnostics.Rd

diagnostics() examines the estimation and interpretation of a fitted mixture model. It assesses convergence and replication across starting values, describes the size and separation of the latent classes, and, where supported, examines associations between indicators that are not adequately represented by the model.

Convergence and likelihood replication indicate whether different starting values lead to the same numerical solution. Class sizes and posterior membership probabilities describe how observations are distributed across classes and how uncertain their classification remains. Bivariate residuals compare observed indicator associations with those implied by the fitted model, helping identify departures from the measurement specification.

The function brings these results together in diagnostic tables and, where available, classification plots. For multilevel models, classification summaries distinguish observation-level profiles from group-level classes. Conditions such as incomplete convergence, estimates at parameter bounds, and classes with no assigned observations are identified for further examination.

Usage

diagnostics(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE, by = c("profile", "overall"), ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model of this package.

data

Optional data frame used to fit the model. When omitted, the required columns are reconstructed from the fitted object.

plots

TRUE (the default) draws classification plots for model families that support them: effective profile sizes, posterior probabilities of assigned profiles, case entropy, and the average posterior probability matrix. If ggplot2 is unavailable or the model family has no classification plots, a message is issued and the tables are returned without plots. FALSE returns only the tables.

by

"profile" (the default) assesses each profile's bivariate residuals separately; "overall" pools them. This argument is forwarded to the residual calculations. The classification levels are determined by the fitted model.

...

Not used. For diagnostics() and plot(), any further argument raises latents_bad_argument; style the returned plots with ggplot2.

Value

An object of class multilpa_diagnostics. The checks table, accessed with get_results(result, "checks"), contains one row per check and columns domain, check, level, value (numeric), display (formatted value), criterion, status, detail and reference. Tables are accessed with get_results(), using what = "checks", "entropy", "classification", "average_posteriors", "residuals", "replication" or "all". A model family without bivariate residuals leaves that table out of "all", and asking for it by name raises latents_no_group_classes; a fit with a noise component has none either, and raises latents_unsupported_noise.

print() groups checks by domain, highlights those requiring review and returns the object invisibly. For supported model families, plot() returns four classification plots as a latents_plots list of ggplot objects; printing the list draws all four plots. as.data.frame() returns the entropy table. summary() returns the diagnostics object.

Details

  • Estimation: convergence of the selected solution; replication of the best log likelihood across completed starts (Masyn, 2013); failed or unfinished starts; and estimates at parameter bounds. Preliminary screening starts are reported separately from full optimisation runs.

  • Class size, at each level the fit classifies: the smallest class, the largest gap between modal and model-estimated class proportions, and classes to which no unit is assigned.

  • Classification: relative entropy (Ramaswamy et al., 1993), which describes classification precision and is not a criterion for the number of classes (Clark & Muthen, 2009); the lowest average posterior probability of the assigned class and the lowest odds of correct classification (Nagin, 2005).

  • Bivariate residuals: discrepancies between observed and model-implied indicator associations, reported under the "Local independence" domain. Where tests are available, pairs are flagged at 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment (Vermunt & Magidson, 2005). Residuals without an available test are reported descriptively.

  • Information: log likelihood, number of parameters and BIC, for comparison with other fitted models using compare_models().

The status labels are "fail" for a non-converged selected solution or a class with effective membership below one; "check" for conditions requiring review, including failed or unfinished starts, active parameter bounds, classes with no modal assignments or residual indicator dependence; "ok" when the checked condition is absent; "info" for a descriptive quantity; and "n/a" for an unavailable or inapplicable quantity. An "ok" status applies only to the specified check and does not establish overall model adequacy. Classification summaries use the fitted posterior probabilities, eligible observations and sampling weights. The available diagnostics depend on the model family.

Entropy, classification and average-posterior tables are supplied at the classification levels supported by each family, together with a summary of replication across starts ("replication"). Group-classified regressions report the group level; hierarchical regression and growth models report both levels. All-empty transition rows follow the fitted drop_empty policy, and zero-weight units are never classified. Bivariate residuals are gathered for families that support them.

Interpretation

Numerical convergence, classification separation, and measurement fit address different aspects of a model. A converged solution may contain poorly separated classes, while sharply separated classes may arise under an inadequate measurement specification. The diagnostics should therefore be interpreted jointly, with attention to the study design and the substantive meaning of the estimated classes.

References

Clark, S. L., & Muthen, B. (2009). Relating latent class analysis results to variables not included in the analysis. Unpublished manuscript.

Masyn, K. E. (2013). Latent class analysis and finite mixture modeling. In T. D. Little (Ed.), The Oxford handbook of quantitative methods (Vol. 2, pp. 551-611). Oxford University Press.

Nagin, D. S. (2005). Group-based modeling of development. Harvard University Press.

Ramaswamy, V., DeSarbo, W. S., Reibstein, D. J., & Robinson, W. T. (1993). An empirical pooling approach for estimating marketing mix elasticities with PIMS data. Marketing Science, 12(1), 103-124. doi:10.1287/mksc.12.1.103

Vermunt, J. K., & Magidson, J. (2005). Latent GOLD 4.0 user's guide. Statistical Innovations.

See also

get_results() for these and the other tables, descriptives() for the variables before fitting, and summary() for the estimates.

Examples

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
quality <- diagnostics(fit, plots = FALSE)
quality
